newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Reefs in Philippine mining merger.
newsitem.headline: Western Reefs in Philippine mining merger.

text.p: Australian miner Western Reefs Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to merge with Trimark Mining Corp (TMC) of the Philippines.

"TMC, which is based on the island of Mindanao, will bring to the company six joint ventures already finalised and documented, five other joint ventures close to agreement, together with a unique system for the granting of exploration permits in the Philippines," Western Reefs said.
Western Reefs said it would issue five million shares to the existing shareholders of TMC on the granting of a minimum of five exploration permits or mineral production sharing agreements.
Western Reef shares were quoted in midday trading at 45 cents each, up two cents from Tuesday's close.
The company also is listed on the Berlin bourse.
The granting of further exploration permits after the first five did not require issuing of further shares, it said,

The objective is to provide an operating base and to negotiate a minimum of 10 joint ventures on properties prospective for precious and base metals including gold, copper and nickel, Western Reefs said.

Following confirmation of attributable economic reserves of gold, or gold equivalent, over the properties, TMC has been provided with an incentive of up to a further five million shares in Western Reefs for two million ounces of gold, or gold equivalent, attributable to Western Reefs.
Western Reefs said it has been actively pursuing mining interests in the Philippines for over 12 months.
"This approach will provide Western Reefs with granted EPs (exploration permits) in the shortest possible time with the least amount of risk," the company said.
Western Reefs holds a 49.9 percent interest in the Dalgaranga gold mine in Western Australia.
